messages:
julian: quick heads-up — ran an nsys + perfetto pass on the staging cluster after the canary. seeing a consistent ~12–18ms spike at the kernel selector stage when batch_size >= 16, even though matmul kernel times look stable. attaching perfetto link and nvtx snippets.

maria: thanks. do you have the nsys cmd you used? want to reproduce locally.

julian: sure — ran: `nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx --output trace_stage1 --sample=cpu --capture-range=nvtx` then uploaded perfetto to the perf infra. main nugget is a bunch of short NVTX ranges around dispatch that seem to serialize (lots of small memcpy + kernel-launch ranges).

sam: can you paste the nvtx annotations you saw? curious if we accidentally added per-request spans that are too fine-grained.

julian: pasted below — it's a condensed timeline extract from perfetto (timestamps removed for thread). see pattern:

```
NVTX push: "req:1234:infer:start"
NVTX push: "selector:choose_kernel:batch=16:policy=latency"
NVTX push: "kernel:matmul:q8_4x4:shapes=16x4096x4096"
NVTX pop
NVTX push: "kvcache:lookup:hit:prefetch=0"
NVTX pop
NVTX push: "memcpy:host->device:small-chunk"
NVTX pop
NVTX push: "kernel:matmul:q8_4x4:launch"
NVTX pop
NVTX pop: "selector:choose_kernel:batch=16:policy=latency"
NVTX pop: "req:1234:infer:end"
```

julian: the odd thing is that instead of coalescing the memcpy + launch windows, perfetto shows gaps where the selector thread is doing decision logic repeatedly per request, not per batch — leading to serialization.

alex: that sounds like batching heuristics not folding request-level spans into a single batch span. are we pushing per-request NVTX push/pop inside the batch loop?

maria: i dug into the code path — in attempt to get per-request tracing we added a `push_range` at request entry and pop at request exit in the request handling loop. but batcher composes batches by moving pointers; it doesn't synthesize a single batched NVTX range. so the selector sees N request ranges inside one batch and emits kernel-choice logs for each request.

sam: oof. that matches the trace. quick mitigation: either 1) change the NVTX convention to have batch-level synthesized ranges (recommended) or 2) make selector emit only once per batch when a batch is materialized.

perf-bot: automated note: perf baseline (master @ 7f9b) vs canary (canary @ d4c2) — 14.2% p95 latency regression on infer route when batch_size >= 16. Regression linked: https://perf.example.internal/regressions/2222101111

maria: proposal for NVTX naming (minimal, parseable): `rl:<request_id>|batch:<batch_id>|phase:<phase>|kernel:<kernel_name>|meta:key=val` where `rl` = request-level, and for batch-synthesized ranges we use `batch:<batch_id>` as the primary top-level tag. example: `batch:42|phase:prepare|kernel:selector` then `batch:42|phase:launch|kernel:matmul_q8`. keeps parsers simple.

julian: +1 for that. also add a `span_id` field when we want to map back to request — but keep it optional so parsers can aggregate by batch_id only.

alex: would prefer `:` separators for readability, e.g. `batch:42/phase:prepare/kernel:selector` but parser friendliness matters. either way we should avoid per-request pushes inside the hot loop.

sam: actionable checklist:
- stop emitting per-request NVTX inside batch hot path (maria)
- synthesize batch-level NVTX ranges in batcher (julian + alex)
- re-run nsys with `--capture-range=nvtx` and check p95 (sam)
- add tests that ensure NVTX coalescing doesn't regress latency (perf-team)

maria: started a PR to hoist the request-level push/pop out of the hot loop and to add a `BatchSpan` helper that does a single push/pop per batch. link: https://git.redwood/infra/runtime/pulls/4287 (WIP)

julian: i'll re-run the perfetto trace and nsys once the PR is in. expectation: remove ~10ms of selector-induced serialization at batch_size 16.

alex: one more note — KV cache lookups are sometimes triggering device-side syncs due to a debug cudaDeviceSynchronize() in the prefetch path (leftover from debugging). i filed a separate issue: https://issues.redwood/internal/12345 — if folks see small memcpy gaps after fixing NVTX they should check that.

sam: thanks all. if PR lands today i'll kick another canary tomorrow morning and run `nsys profile` + quick flame diff. please @channel if you spot anything blocking. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: reminder: keep traces anonymized before sharing externally.
